title: The aim
text:
Warhammer 40,000. You each command an army. You take a whole turn, five phases, then your opponent does. That is one battle round. A full game is five; a tutorial is three.

You win on victory points, and victory points come from holding objectives. Destroying things is a means. I mention this now because everyone forgets it by round two.

title: The datasheet
text:
Pick up one unit's datasheet. Movement, Toughness, Save, Wounds, Leadership, Objective Control. Then a weapon: attacks, the number it needs to hit, Strength, AP, Damage.

Those are the only numbers you will use for the next hour. I do not hold them. They are on your datasheet, and they change.

title: Table and terrain
text: Terrain goes on the footprints your mission shows. In this edition the objectives are inside the terrain, so the ruins are the prize, not just the hiding place.

title: Deploy
text:
Roll off. The winner chooses a deployment zone and places a unit first. Alternate until everything is down.

Some units arrive later from reserve, or deploy by rules of their own. Their datasheets say so. Ask me when you reach one.

title: Who goes first
text:
Roll off again. The winner decides who takes the first turn. Going first attacks earlier. Going second scores last. There is no wrong answer, only consequences.

If it is not the player I have named, tap Swap first.

title: Command phase
text:
Both players gain one command point in every Command phase, whoever's turn it is. I add them.

Battle-shock tests are only for units below half strength. There are none yet. Then any command abilities on your datasheets.

That is all. It gets longer later.

title: Movement phase
text:
Each unit may make a normal move up to its Movement, Advance for one extra die of inches, or stay put. Keep each model within two inches of a friend. Measure from base to base.

A unit that starts beside the enemy may Fall Back instead. Reserves arrive in this phase.

Tell me the first time you Advance or Fall Back.

title: Shooting phase
text:
Pick a unit and a target it can see. Roll to hit: one die per attack, needing the hit number or more. Cover takes one off the roll. A one always misses; a six always hits.

Roll to wound: Strength against Toughness. The chart is under Cards. Your opponent rolls a save for each wound, made worse by your AP. Each failed save does the weapon's Damage to one model.

title: Charge phase
text:
Pick a unit within twelve inches of an enemy. Roll two dice: that is how far it may charge. Then name targets inside that distance, and move so at least one model ends within two inches of each.

Your opponent may spend a command point to shoot the charging unit first. Those shots hit only on sixes.

Tell me the first time you charge.

title: Your first charge
text:
A unit that Advanced or Fell Back this turn may not charge. If the dice fall short of every target, the charge fails and the unit stays where it is.

A unit that charged fights first in the Fight phase. That is the reward for the walk.

title: Fight phase
text:
Everyone in combat piles in three inches first. Units that charged fight first. Then you take turns choosing a unit to fight, starting with the player whose turn it is not.

It is the same loop: hit on the weapon's number, wound, save, damage. At the end, everyone consolidates three inches.

title: The other turn
text:
That turn is over. Now the other player takes the same five phases: Command, Movement, Shooting, Charge, Fight. I will announce each.

When both of you have had a turn, the battle round ends.

title: Scoring begins
text:
Round two. From now on most missions score at the start of your own Command phase. For each objective you control, take the points your mission gives. You control it when you have more Objective Control inside it than they do.

Tap Score and give me the number. What matters is what you hold when your own turn begins.

title: Battle-shock
text:
A unit below half strength takes a battle-shock test in its own Command phase. Roll two dice. At or above its Leadership, it passes.

Fail, and it holds nothing and uses no stratagems. In this edition it stays shocked until it passes a later test.

Mark it under Army, and I will remind you.

title: Stratagems
text:
You spent a command point. A stratagem is a one-off trick that costs one or two of them. Your cards say what each does.

The rule to remember: one stratagem on a unit in a phase, and never the same stratagem twice in a phase.

title: Advancing
text: An Advance adds one die of inches to the unit's move. In return the unit may not charge this turn, and only its Assault weapons may fire.

title: Falling back
text: Falling Back takes a unit out of a fight. It costs that unit its shooting and its charge this turn, unless its datasheet says otherwise.

title: The final round
text:
Final round. Score at the start of your Command phase, as before. At the end of the game most missions give points for what you still hold.

Everything else is theatre.

title: What to learn next
text:
The full game adds two rounds, secondary objectives drawn from a deck, and your detachment's own stratagems.

After that: reserves and deep strike, units that fight first, leaders joining units, vehicles and monsters, and how your army's disposition picks the mission.

You know the loop. The rest is reading.
